newsitem.title: USA: Justice Dept. probes FCC airwaves auctions.
newsitem.headline: Justice Dept. probes FCC airwaves auctions.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department is investigating possible rigging of bids at recent airwaves auctions held by the federal government.
Documents obtained by Reuters Wednesday show that the department's antitrust division also is looking into the illegal allocation of wireless telephone licenses.

The department's probe appears to focus on the Federal Communications Commission auction that ended in mid-January and raised $2.5 billion for the government. At that auction, the FCC sold the rights for a new generation of cellular phone service known as "personal communications services."
An attorney familiar with the investigation said the department has sent out "numerous" letters requesting information from auction participants.

The "civil investigative demand" seeks information about a company's bidding strategies, its communications about the auction with other telecommunications firms, and other material. Top bidders at the January sale were units of Sprint Corp., AT&T Corp. and BellSouth Corp. It was not immediately known whether these companies were the focus of the probe.
A Justice Department spokeswoman was not immediately available for comment.
